predecessors.name: Allied-occupied Germany
predecessors.text: the Soviet occupation zone, "the Soviet Occupation Zone (Sowjetische Besatzungszone, SBZ) comprised the five states", with East Berlin

successors.name: Germany (reunified)
successors.text: the five re-established states of Brandenburg, Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, Saxony, Saxony-Anhalt and Thuringia, with East Berlin united with West Berlin

rulers.name: Walter Ulbricht
rulers.title: First Secretary of the SED (de facto leader)

ledger.x: 1949: the SED establishes the German Democratic Republic in the Soviet zone, with East Berlin as capital.
1990: the five East German states join the Federal Republic.

1990: the GDR is absorbed into the Federal Republic, which "continued to exist under the same legal personality that was founded in May 1949" (Cliopatria draws the enlarged state as the Federated Republic of Germany from 1991).
1990: the GDR ceases to exist on 3 October.

wars.name: Berlin Crisis of 1961
wars.outcome: No territory changed hands: "the GDR closed the inner German border" and "on the night of 12 August 1961, East German soldiers began erecting the Berlin Wall" (infobox "Berlin Crisis: 4 June 1961"); East Berlin was made the 15th Bezirk in 1961.

certainty.note: The GDR's whole outline was fixed: the Oder-Neisse line to Poland (Potsdam 1945, recognised by the GDR in the 1950 Treaty of Zgorzelec and again by the 1990 German-Polish Border Treaty), the Czech frontier, the Baltic coast, and the inner…
